bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42475209 (freetype2): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target pdf_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42475209
bug_description.normalized: The staged PDF witness is accepted by poppler and reaches FreeType's scalable outline path while rendering text. The saved MemorySanitizer stack contains two recursive `load_truetype_glyph` frames at `src/truetype/ttgload.c:2064` before the crashing `TT_Process_Simple_Glyph` frame, so the buggy call operates on a simple TrueType component glyph reached during composite expansion rather than proving that the top-level glyph handed to `FT_Load_Glyph` is itself simple. In vulnerable `TT_Process_Simple_Glyph`, local pointer `unrounded` is declared without initialization and is assigned only inside the variation-font branch `FT_IS_NAMED_INSTANCE(...) || FT_IS_VARIATION(...)`. On the witnessed default-instance component path that branch is not taken, so `unrounded` keeps its indeterminate stack value, but the render load still has scaling enabled because `FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE` is not set. The later `do_scale` loop nonetheless rescales glyph points from `unrounded`, and the first `FT_MulDiv( unrounded->x, ... )` read at `src/truetype/ttgload.c:1056` triggers the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value. The fix in commit `94ebc248653ede802b2bfbf6219e17f487fab3ff` moves `IS_DEFAULT_INSTANCE` into shared scope, allocates temporary `unrounded` storage only for non-default variation fonts, and scales default-instance glyphs directly from `outline->points` instead of the uninitialized pointer.

source.description: First project-side read that creates the vulnerability-relevant recursive load state. `TT_Load_Composite_Glyph` reads a component glyph index from attacker-controlled composite-glyph data; the saved recursive `load_truetype_glyph` frames show that this component selection leads to the crashing simple-glyph call.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled bytes from the embedded TrueType composite glyph data reached during rendering of the staged PDF. While parsing a composite record from the font's `glyf` table, FreeType materializes `subglyph->index`, which the loader later recurses on at `load_truetype_glyph( ..., subglyph->index, ... )`.

root_cause.description: Missing default-instance guard around the scaling loop. `unrounded` is initialized only on the variation-font path, but this loop still chooses it as the source coordinate array whenever `do_scale` is true. On the witnessed default-instance component path reached during composite expansion, the loop therefore carries an indeterminate stack pointer into the dereference at the sink. The fix adds an `IS_DEFAULT_INSTANCE` split here and scales default-instance outlines from `vec` directly.

sink.description: MSAN sink. The scaling loop dereferences `unrounded->x` through the indeterminate pointer carried from the default-instance component path. The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/truetype/ttgload.c:1056:42` in this expression.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state is the uninitialized stack pointer `unrounded`. The function declares it without an initializer, and only the variation-font branch later assigns it before the scaling code.

parser_admitted.description: The crashing path enters FreeType's composite-glyph parser before the recursive component loads seen in the saved stack. This call reads attacker-controlled component records from `glyf`, after which line 2064 recurses into the selected component glyphs.

coarse_trace.summary: On the witnessed path FreeType is parsing a composite glyph: it reads an attacker-controlled component record from `glyf` and materializes `subglyph->index` for a nested component.
Composite expansion recursively calls `load_truetype_glyph` on that component, and the saved MemorySanitizer stack shows two recursive frames at line 2064 before the crashing simple-glyph frame.
In the recursive component load, `TT_Load_Glyph_Header` reads a positive contour count and `load_truetype_glyph` routes that component through the simple-glyph branch into `TT_Process_Simple_Glyph`.
The function declares local pointer `unrounded`, skips its only assignment on the default-instance path, and still enables scaling because `FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE` is unset.
The unguarded `do_scale` loop uses `unrounded` as the source coordinate array anyway, and the first `unrounded->x` read matches the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value at line 1056.

fine_trace.note: Source. While parsing a composite glyph record, FreeType reads the attacker-controlled component glyph index that will be expanded recursively on the crashing path.

Composite expansion recurses into the component selected in step 1. The saved sanitizer stack shows two `load_truetype_glyph` frames at this line before the crashing frame at line 1798, so the buggy `TT_Process_Simple_Glyph` invocation operates on a recursively loaded component glyph.

In that recursive component load, FreeType reads the component glyph's signed contour count from attacker-controlled `glyf` data. On the witnessed path this value is positive, which is the state later used to select simple-glyph processing.

The positive contour count from step 3 selects the simple-glyph branch for this recursively loaded component. After the outline body is loaded, that branch dispatches into `TT_Process_Simple_Glyph` at line 1798.
The local pointer that later feeds scaling is declared without initialization. Unless a later branch assigns it, this stack slot remains indeterminate throughout the rest of the function.

This is the only assignment site for `unrounded`. On the witnessed default-instance component path this predicate is false, so the pointer remains unchanged from step 5 instead of being bound to `gloader->current.extra_points2`.

The crashing render request is a scaled outline load. Poppler's `getFTLoadFlags()` starts from `FT_LOAD_DEFAULT`, and the `FT_Load_Glyph` call at `SplashFTFont.cc:299` uses those flags without adding `FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE`, so this branch copies the size metrics and sets `do_scale = TRUE`.

Root cause. Once step 7 sets `do_scale`, the loop unconditionally uses `unrounded` as the source coordinate array. There is no default-instance branch here to fall back to `vec`, so the indeterminate pointer from steps 5 and 6 is carried into its increment and dereference path.

fine_trace.code:
vec->x = FT_MulDiv( unrounded->x, x_scale, 0x10000L * 64 );
vec->y = FT_MulDiv( unrounded->y, y_scale, 0x10000L * 64 );
fine_trace.note: Sink. The first loop iteration dereferences `unrounded->x` and then `unrounded->y` through the indeterminate pointer selected in step 8. The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/truetype/ttgload.c:1056:42` in this expression.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix changes this exact `TT_Process_Simple_Glyph` region by making `unrounded` variation-only, introducing `IS_DEFAULT_INSTANCE( FT_FACE( loader->face ) )`, and adding a separate default-instance scaling branch that no longer dereferences the uninitialized pointer. Stage 02 did not run the fixed image.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42475209 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `/out/pdf_fuzzer` and reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `TT_Process_Simple_Glyph`. The saved stack contains the crashing `load_truetype_glyph` simple-glyph frame at `ttgload.c:1798`, preceded by two recursive `load_truetype_glyph` component-load frames at `ttgload.c:2064`, before returning to `TT_Load_Glyph`.

format.name: PDF that reaches a simple default-instance TrueType component glyph during recursive composite loading
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged witness `poc` (sha256 `d6efb01d721dd9c73c219b61cabcd24db68aa05d481c961d2b66aa7d49fbde3e`) as rendered by `pdf_fuzzer`. On this witness, poppler must accept the PDF, reach text rendering, and hand FreeType an outline load whose expansion descends through the two recursive `load_truetype_glyph` component-load frames saved at `ttgload.c:2064` before `TT_Process_Simple_Glyph` runs on a simple TrueType component glyph. On that crashing component path, the face stays on the default-instance path (the only assignment predicate `FT_IS_NAMED_INSTANCE(...) || FT_IS_VARIATION(...)` is false) and scaling remains enabled (`FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE` unset). Those exact local properties make `TT_Process_Simple_Glyph` skip the only assignment to `unrounded` but still enter the `do_scale` loop, so line 1056 reads `unrounded->x` before the pointer has been initialized.
